arm_C_host_auc.sd_note: sd_population is the one quoted in the verdict and in STATUS.md; the sample SD is 0.0900. The conclusion is the same either way, and the comparison with the A/B cluster's 0.0013 (also population) is like for like. vamp flagged the ambiguity on 2026-10-24.

deciding_statistic: escape rate, AUC > 0.25; ship rule was escapes >= 3/4 on the new seeds AND one seed beating the best A/B run by > 0.05 AUC

def_arms_lost.cause: my error, and a specific one. gate_launch.sh arms a DETACHED host-side watchdog at box creation -- for that box, --max-hours 3. I later extended my own independent backstop from 05:26 to 06:20 to cover D/E/F, but never touched the launcher's, which was the earlier authority and fired first. I had checked for a watchdog ON THE BOX, found only the kernel's watchdogd, and concluded there was none; it runs on this host, not on the instance.
def_arms_lost.cost: about 1.1 GPU-hours, roughly $0.77, and four runs that were descriptive by design.
def_arms_lost.fixes: brev/launch_ab350.sh now counts every process holding a `brev delete <name>` timer, reports when the earliest fires, and refuses to start a cell whose earliest authority fires before the run can finish. It also pulls results every 10 minutes instead of only at DONE.
def_arms_lost.not_being_rerun: D/E/F at two seeds cannot clear 0.05 whatever they show (Fisher 2/2 vs 0/4 = 0.067), so re-running them would buy a descriptive line for about $1.20 and 1.7 h. The budget is better spent on the 3-clip A/B. Flagged rather than quietly dropped.
def_arms_lost.what_happened: the sweep box was deleted at about 04:55 UTC on 2026-10-25 with 8 of 10 runs finished and only the 4 arm C runs pulled. D/E/F runs 5-8 (D_s44, E_s44, F_s44 and probably D_s45) completed on the box and were lost with it, together with their kept policies.
def_arms_lost.what_was_not_lost: arm C, the only arm whose escape rate could clear 0.05 at this allocation, was complete, pulled, scored and committed before the deletion. The verdict above does not change.

selection_signal.caveat: n=6 for the correlation and n=4 for the confirmation seeds; both are small, and this is reported as measured rather than as established.
selection_signal.consequence: seed and checkpoint selection for Tier 2 has to happen on our own synthetic noise, which is what the brief's dev/confirm split already required. There is no legitimate shortcut through either the evaluator metric or the Tier 1 reference.
selection_signal.finding: no. The evaluator's own AUC, computed against the corrupted Tier 2 input the policy was given, does not track the clean-reference score across C's seeds: Spearman -0.60 on the four new seeds and -0.14 over all six. At n=6 that is not significant either way, so the honest statement is that the evaluator metric carries no usable selection signal here.
selection_signal.not_explained: I first wrote that the sign was what arm C's mechanism predicts. vamp corrected that and is right: ws/residual amendment 3 has C relaxing VOC inside the bound, which predicts how OFTEN a run escapes, not that an escaped run tracks the clean reference better than it tracks its own training target. Nothing in the arm's stated mechanism predicts this sign. It is recorded as measured and unexplained.
selection_signal.question: can seeds be chosen without touching the clean Tier 1 reference, which the brief forbids as supervision?

verdict.kept_for_the_record: arm A stays the reference recipe for the full pass. C is not discarded, it is unproven.
verdict.the_arm_is_bimodal_both_ways: C_s46 scored 0.1821, BELOW every A and B run, and its MPPE 24.3 cm is worse than A's 18.8 cm. The correction does not only add upside; it can also cost.
verdict.why: the pre-registered rule needed >= 3/4 escapes on the confirmation seeds and got 2/4 (Fisher one-sided 0.214). Over all six seeds the rate is 3/6 at Fisher 0.167. C's mean AUC 0.2666 is above the A/B cluster at 0.2016, but its own SD is 0.0821 against the cluster's 0.0013, so the mean is not the statistic that decides this and the escape rate did not clear the bar.

what: arm C (bounded object-target correction) at four more seeds on e24, 10M steps, gated-cleaned Tier 2 reference
